item.title: Digital Health Week highlights online tools for Islanders
item.description:
Digital Health Week highlights online tools for Islanders jenniferdhogan Mon, 11/16/2026 - 11:17

During Digital Health Week, November 16 to 22, Islanders are encouraged to explore trusted digital tools and resources that help them access health information and take a more active role in their health.

Digital Health Week is an annual national initiative led by Canada Health Infoway. This year’s focus is on connected care, highlighting the importance of a patient’s health information moving securely between various providers and care settings.

In Prince Edward Island, MyHealthPEI, an online tool recently introduced, gives Island residents aged 16 and older secure access to laboratory results, diagnostic imaging reports, immunization records, self-entry tools and trusted educational health information.

“Digital health investments are giving Islanders more secure and convenient access to their health information, while helping health-care providers deliver more connected and coordinated care. The first year of MyHealthPEI has shown that Islanders value having greater access to their health information and opportunities to participate more actively in their care.”

-Health and Wellness Minister, Cory Deagle

As of November 1, 2026, more than 16,000 Islanders have registered for MyHealthPEI and connected to their personal health information online. Islanders who are not yet using it can create and verify a MyPEI account and connect to MyHealthPEI using a valid PEI Health Card.

This week, participating PEI Public Libraries will offer in-person clinics to help people with MyPEI account setup, verification and MyHealthPEI access. Islanders should review the identification requirements and bring the necessary documents. Year-round support is also available at Access PEI locations. Information on pop-up clinic locations and required documents is available online. 

“We know that having someone available to help can make a real difference when people are getting started with digital health tools,” said MyHealthPEI manager of Citizen Information Services Kelly Coughlin. “By partnering with PEI Public Libraries, Access PEI and community organizations, we are bringing support closer to Islanders and making it easier for them to connect with digital health services.”

Prince Edward Island’s participation in Digital Health Week reflects the province’s five-year Digital Health Strategy, which guides investments in secure technologies that help Islanders manage their health, support providers in delivering care and strengthen the use of health information across the system.

Schedule for pop-up clinics at PEI Public Libraries:

  • Charlottetown Public Library – Monday, November 16 from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m.
  • Summerside Public Library – Wednesday, November 18 from 1 p.m. to 3 p.m.
  • Souris Public Library – Thursday, November 19 from 10 a.m. to 12 p.m.
  • Montague Public Library – Thursday, November 19 from 2 p.m. to 4 p.m.
  • O’Leary Public Library – Friday, November 20 from 1 p.m. to 3 p.m.

Quick facts:

As of November 1, 2026, more than 16,000 MyHealthPEI accounts have been created. Islanders have used the service to:

  • View recent laboratory results more than 365,000 times 
  • View recent diagnostic imaging reports more than 187,000 times 
  • View immunization histories more than 40,000 times 
  • Record more than 87,000 updates using self-entry health tools, with the highest self-entry updates: health issues (14,700), medical procedures (14,500), allergy information (8,400), and blood pressure measurements (6,500). 
  • Upload more than 8,400 personal medical documents
  • Print more than 11,000 documents

item.title: Health PEI prepares for upcoming Accreditation Canada surveys
item.description:
Health PEI prepares for upcoming Accreditation Canada surveys jenniferdhogan Mon, 11/16/2026 - 10:17

Health PEI is preparing for its upcoming Accreditation Canada on-site survey visits, scheduled for November 2026 and June 2027, as part of its ongoing commitment to delivering safe, high-quality, person-centered care for Islanders.

From November 22 to 27, 2026, Accreditation Canada surveyors will visit many Health PEI facilities and programs across Prince Edward Island. During this time, surveyors will meet with staff, physicians, leaders, volunteers, patients, clients, residents and their families, to gain a firsthand understanding of the care and services being delivered throughout the organization.

Accreditation is an important part of organizational accountability and continuous quality improvement. Through its partnership with the Health Standards Organization (HSO) and Accreditation Canada, Health PEI assesses its programs and services against evidence-based national standards to strengthen quality, safety, and patient experience across the health system.

"Accreditation is more than a survey visit. It is an ongoing journey of learning, collaboration and improvement that helps ensure we continue providing the highest quality care possible to Islanders. We look forward to welcoming surveyors to our facilities and programs this November and demonstrating the dedication and expertise of our teams across the organization."

- Chief Executive Officer of Health PEI, Laurae Kloschinsky

The surveys will assess Health PEI programs and services against national standards and provide valuable insights into organizational strengths and opportunities for improvement. Surveyors will be visible in facilities and programs across the province, observing care environments, reviewing practices, and speaking with both our teams and the patients, clients, residents and families we serve about quality and safety initiatives.

Following the June 2027 survey visit, Health PEI will receive a report and will be awarded an accreditation decision in summer of 2027.

Health PEI's last on-site accreditation survey took place in 2022. Since then, teams across the organization have continued to advance initiatives aimed at enhancing patient safety, quality of care, and service delivery. Accreditation findings and final decisions are shared publicly, reinforcing transparency and accountability to Islanders.

"Accreditation involves everyone," said Laurae Kloschinsky. "It is an opportunity to celebrate the exceptional work happening across Health PEI every day, learn from one another, and demonstrate our ongoing commitment to providing safe, high-quality care and services for Islanders."

As Health PEI prepares to welcome surveyors, the organization extends its thanks to staff, physicians, volunteers, patient and family partners, leaders, foundations, unions, and community partners whose ongoing commitment to quality and patient safety helps ensure the best possible care for Islanders.

item.title: Nominations open for PEI Anti-Racism Recognition Award
item.description:
Nominations open for PEI Anti-Racism Recognition Award jpranahan Fri, 11/13/2026 - 12:15

Island residents are invited to nominate individuals, community groups and organizations that are making a difference in addressing racism and promoting racial equity across Prince Edward Island. 

The Anti-Racism Recognition Award recognizes leadership, advocacy and community efforts that help remove barriers, promote inclusion and create positive change for racialized and Indigenous communities.

Nominations are open until December 14, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. AST.

Individuals, community groups and organizations may be nominated for their contributions to advancing anti-racism, racial equity, inclusion or reconciliation in Prince Edward Island.

The award was established through the Anti-Racism Action Plan for Prince Edward Island 2023-2028 as part of the province’s commitment to recognizing efforts to address racism.

The inaugural award was presented in February 2026 to Tamara Steele, former executive director and board member of the Black Cultural Society of PEI, in recognition of her longstanding leadership, advocacy and contributions to racial justice on the Island. 

To learn more about the eligibility criteria or to submit a nomination, visit here.

For questions about the award or nomination process, contact the Anti-Racism Office at antiracismtable@gov.pe.ca.

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
Media and Communications Coordinator
Cabinet Communications and Protocol
Government of the Northwest Territories
